item.title: Summer Camp Spots Still Available for CRPD Fitness Camp!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Sign Up Today for CRPD Fitness Camp!

CRPD Fitness Camp is an eight-week, day-long camp that is so much fun for campers ages five to 15! Students participate in a variety of activities, from fitness training, sports, swimming lessons, group games, creative arts and more.

There are still slots available for campers at Blackburn, Douglas and Glenwood community centers. Camp hours are 7 a.m.-6 p.m. from June 13-Aug. 5. Campers must have completed kindergarten by June 6 of this year and be no older than 15 by that date. 

You can register your kids at 1111 E. Broad St., Monday-Friday from 8 a.m.-5 p.m. until Friday, May 13. Please bring the application and requested documents.

Learn more about CRPD Fitness Camp.

item.title: Fitness Camp Openings
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

SPACE IS STILL AVAILABLE

Fitness camp is 8 weeks of fun and active programming focused on improving the physical, mental, social and emotional health of your child aged 5-15! Don’t miss out on getting your child enrolled now! We have spots open at our Glenwood and Douglas location. Please click here to register for these locations. 

  • Credit card and debit card payments are the only types of payments accepted (online and in-person). 
  • Payment options are available: $100 per child at time of registration and $95 per child no later than July 6th. Full payment of $195 can be made at time of registration online through Activenet. 
    • Once you complete your registration form and submit your documentation, you can request payment arrangements by calling Katie Teggart at 614-645-0702.
  • Your 2020 Federal 1040 tax form filed with the IRS and child's birth certificate must be uploaded to the registration form. If you filed "Married Filing Separately" both spouse's 2020 1040 tax forms must be submitted. No other documentation is accepted. 
    • Please check our Fitness Camp website for income guidelines. 

If you have any questions, please call 614-645-0702. 
columbus.gov/fitnesscamp/

614-645-3950

item.description:

Summer 2021

Hello CRPD Fitness Camp Families:

I hope this email finds you safe and healthy! Registration for Fitness Camp is almost here!

Online registration starts Saturday, April 24, at 10 a.m. Space is limited to the first 25 registrations per location. Please visit CRPDCamps.com to view the new online registration process, income eligibility requirements, fees and more.

In-person registration takes place April 26 - May 13, Monday through Thursday, from 11 a.m.-1 p.m. and 5-7 p.m., as long as spaces are available.

 

In-person registration - and fitness camps - are held at the following community centers:

Blackburn | 263 Carpenter St., 43205
Douglas | 1250 Windsor Ave., 43211
Driving Park | 1100 Rhoads Ave., 43206
Glenwood | 1888 Fairmont Ave., 43223

Camp Details

Dates:   June 7 - July 30

Hours: 7 a.m.-6 p.m.  (AM Drop off: 7-9 a.m. | PM Pick up: 4-6 p.m.)

 

Cost: $195

Full payment can be made through Activenet, our online registration system, after registration forms have been submitted. Payment plans can be made by calling (614) 645-0702 or (614) 645-3950. The payment plan option will consist of $100 per camper, paid at registration, with the remainder of $95 per camper paid no later than July 6. All payments must be made by credit/debit card. No cash or money orders will be accepted. For any further questions or concerns please email us at CRPDFitness@Columbus.gov.

We look forward for you to join us again this summer!

 

Katie Teggart
Health & Wellness Program Supervisor 

Bryana Ross
Health & Wellness Manager

item.title: Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation is part of The Big Give - Can you Help?
item.description:
Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation is part of The Big Give - Can you Help?

Join us in celebrating the establishment of the Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation - a (501(c)(3) - by donating to the Big Give! The Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation works hand-in-hand with the Columbus Recreation and Parks Department and community volunteers to ensure all residents have access to recreational programs, facilities, places and spaces that make our lives and communities great.

The Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation has teamed up with The Columbus Foundation for its Big Give on June 10.

The Big Give is a one-day online giving event to provide critical financial support to area nonprofits. The Columbus Foundation and its donors have provided a $1.5 million Bonus Pool to be amplified on a prorated basis across all gifts made during The Big Give. This means your donation will be automatically increased by the bonus pool.

If you are able, please consider making a donation to the Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation during The Big Give. The money will be donated to the Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation’s PLAY Grant Program. This program provides sports opportunities to financially challenged children in Columbus.

Last year, over 3,000 vulnerable kids were able to participate in the department’s programs such as soccer, tennis, gymnastics, football and more thanks to donations from this community. We know the need will be even greater this coming year.

If you are able, please make your tax-deductible donation online and help kids in this community. 

For the Webster family, karate was a family affair. Click on the image to watch a video about how this dad and his sons were all able to learn karate thanks to funds provided by the Columbus Recreation and Parks Foundation.

item.title: CRPD Fitness Camp Registration- June 1st!
item.description:
CRPD Fitness Camp- Summer 2020

Hello CRPD Fitness Camp Families:

I hope this email finds all of you safe and healthy! Due to guidelines from Columbus Public Health and new safety protocols created by our department, Columbus Recreation and Parks has made important changes to the CRPD Fitness Camp program.

The locations of our camps have changed to the following sites:

Berliner Athletic Complex | 1300 Deckenbach Rd., 43223
Cleo Dumaree Athletic Complex | 276 S. Nelson Rd., 43205
Willis Athletic Complex | 2520 Mock Rd., 43219

Registration will open on Monday, June 1st at 9:30 AM. Please visit https://www.columbus.gov/crpdfitnesscamp/ to view the new online registration process, income eligibility, adjusted fees and more.

Fitness Camp will be a seven-week program, taking place Monday, June 15 through Friday, July 31 from 8 AM - 5 PM, Monday through Friday. Morning drop off is 8-9 AM and afternoon pick up is 4-5 PM. Daily activities will take place on a rotated schedule, between 9 AM - 4 PM.

Campers will participate in a variety of activities designed to promote skills, confidence and enjoyment with physical activity, in addition to mindfulness and overall wellness. These activities include sports and fitness skills and drills, games and creative arts.

Fee:

$170 | Full payment can be made through our online registration system after your registration form has been submitted. Payment plans can be made by calling (614) 645-3950. The payment plan option will consist of $100 per camper, paid at registration, with the remainder of $70 per camper paid no later than July 13. All payments must be made by credit/debit card.

Due to ordered guidelines for ratios and spacing we will only be taking 32 campers per site.

To ensure the safety of our campers and staff, we will use the athletic complexes and the surrounding park areas for activities, and only registered camp participants and CRPD staff will be allowed to enter Fitness Camp sites.

One reusable cloth face covering will be provided per week as well, as they are required for every camper. Face coverings must be washed daily after camp. Hand wash and air dry are strongly recommended. While wearing a face covering is necessary, we will make exceptions during high-intensity activities (with appropriate social distancing) and for those campers with documented medical and/or breathing conditions.

Full details about the new Columbus Recreation and Parks safety protocols and procedures will be included with this year’s camp information handbook for parents. Learn more about what we’re doing to keep campers safe at columbus.gov/RecParksCOVID19/.

We understand that you may have questions or concerns about these changes. Please email me at CRPDFitness@Columbus.gov for more information. You can also visit our website anytime at columbus.gov/RecParksCOVID19/ for additional details about how we are safely re-opening to serve our community.

 

Thanks!

Bryana Ross
Health & Wellness Manager
Columbus Recreation and Parks

Health and Wellness Office

item.title: Special Live-Stream Forum with Mayor Ginther
Help keep our parks and trails healthy and safe
item.description:
Residents Urged to Play Safe, Live Smart to Stay Healthy and Help Keep Columbus’ Parks and Trails Safe

Visiting Columbus Recreation and Park Department’s trails and parks are a great way to maintain your physical and mental health, but it’s important to Play Safe, Live Smart and take steps to use them safely.

Columbus’ trails and parks currently are open during the coronavirus (COVID-19) public health emergency. Our trails and parks are a resource to help residents enjoy the outdoors while engaging in recreation, exercise and education.

“In these times of great disruption, the health and safety of our residents is key. We have the ability to slow the spread of COVID-19 by rigorously practicing social distancing,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “Encouraging residents to use our trails and parks in a safe way helps prevent exposure and maintains access to these important resources.”

As the City of Columbus takes steps to protect residents and stop the spread of COVID-19, City leaders have carefully weighed the benefits and risks to public health of keeping facilities open.  At this time, the City is committed to keeping parks and trails open as long as it remains safe to do so.

While most residents are practicing social distancing at Columbus’ trails and parks, there are some areas where people are not doing as good of a job, including Antrim Park and the Olentangy Trail.

Play Safe, Life Smart: Practicing Social Distancing at Columbus Trails and Parks

Here are some tips to practice social distancing at Columbus' trails and parks:

Do visit parks and trails with your immediate family and those with whom you’re staying at home.

Do take advantage of opportunities to enjoy the outdoors for recreation, exercise and education.

Do pay attention to signage and barriers that restrict access to equipment, such as playgrounds, tennis courts, disc golf courses and basketball courts.

Do maintain a six-foot distance from others when walking, running and biking. You can do this by letting people know you are passing when you come up from behind and safely stepping off the path to let others pass.

Do NOT use parks or trails if you are exhibiting COVID-19 symptoms.

Do NOT step over or remove any barriers that block access to equipment, facilities and parking lots.

Do NOT play group sports using shared equipment, such as basketball, disc golf and tennis.

Do NOT use any equipment such as picnic tables, playgrounds, and basketball, disc golf and tennis courts. Currently, all recreation equipment is closed.

For additional information about COVID-19, visit Columbus Public Health, Ohio Department of Health or Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Additionally, Ohio residents with specific questions related to COVID-19 can also call 833-4-ASK-ODH (833-427-5634). For a full list of department-related updates and closures, visit ColumbusRecParks.com.
